questions.q: In "no more than 15 minutes of data loss, operational again within one hour," which number is RPO and which is RTO?
options: 15 minutes of data loss is the RPO (Recovery Point Objective); one hour to be operational is the RTO (Recovery Time Objective)
15 minutes is the RTO and one hour is the RPO
Both numbers describe the same thing — RPO and RTO are interchangeable terms
Neither number relates to RPO or RTO — those only apply to backup frequency
questions.explain: RPO measures acceptable data loss in time; RTO measures acceptable downtime — naming both correctly is the first real step.

questions.q: Why does an RTO of one hour rule out a manual failover process?
options: There isn't time for someone to be paged, log in, and manually reconfigure connection strings within that window — failover has to be automatic, pointing to Auto-Failover Groups
Manual failover is actually faster than automatic failover in every case
RTO has no real relationship to how failover is triggered
A one-hour RTO means failover is not needed at all
questions.explain: The business constraint directly rules specific architecture choices in or out — this is the whole point of naming RPO/RTO before picking a technology.

questions.q: Why does the regional-disaster detail specifically rule out relying on local backups alone?
options: A backup stored in the same region as the primary doesn't survive that region having an outage — geo-redundant storage or a cross-region secondary is needed
Local backups are always slower to restore than any other option
Regional disasters never actually affect backup storage
Local backups are only useful for compliance, not disaster recovery
questions.explain: A regional disaster is exactly the scenario where co-located local backups fail to provide real protection.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does "the app reconnected after failover" NOT prove by itself?
options: That recovery actually succeeded — DBCC CHECKDB, row count/checksum comparison, listener-endpoint verification, and timing the whole event against the real targets are all still required
That the failover group exists at all
That the application has any database to connect to
Nothing — app reconnection alone is sufficient proof of full recovery
questions.explain: An app reconnecting is a necessary but not sufficient signal — several more checks are needed before genuinely calling the environment recovered.
